---
title: "What's the way to fix it so it flies sensibly?"
---

{{< include _model.qmd >}}

```{python}
# A stable glider trims at a fixed angle of attack whatever its speed, so the
# only lever on the launch pull-up is trim SPEED. Nose ballast raises it.
EXTRA = 1.0e-3  # kg of lead added at the nose, beyond what trim needs
CLEAN = dict(alpha=15.0, theta=180.0)  # no stall, no loop

opt = optimise(static_margin=0.10)
plane, layout = design_geometry(opt)
fixed = glide(plane, layout, ballast=opt["ballast"] + EXTRA)


def flies_clean(s):
    return (s["alpha_max"] < CLEAN["alpha"]
            and float(np.max(np.abs(s["theta"]))) < CLEAN["theta"])


before = simulate(plane, layout, ballast=opt["ballast"], launch_angle=45)
after = {a: simulate(plane, layout, ballast=opt["ballast"] + EXTRA, launch_angle=a)
         for a in [10, 20, 30]}
best = max((s for s in after.values() if flies_clean(s)), key=lambda s: s["duration"])
turn = lambda s: float(np.max(np.abs(s["theta"])))  # noqa: E731

assert not flies_clean(before)                       # it loops as delivered
assert flies_clean(best)                             # and does not, ballasted
assert fixed["V"] > opt["V"]                         # via a higher trim speed
assert fixed["sink"] > opt["sink"]                   # which is what it costs
assert not flies_clean(after[30])                    # angle matters too
```

::: {.hero}
[`{python} f"+{EXTRA*1e3:.1f} g"`]{.hero-value}
[nose ballast; the loop disappears]{.hero-label}
:::

**Answer.** Raise the trim speed toward the throw. A stable glider holds one
angle of attack at any speed, so at
[`{python} f"{V_LAUNCH/opt['V']:.1f}"`×]{.key} trim it must make several times
its weight in lift. `{python} f"{EXTRA*1e3:.1f}"` g of nose lead takes trim from
`{python} f"{opt['V']:.1f}"` to [`{python} f"{fixed['V']:.1f}"` m/s]{.key}
(@tbl-fix), and α now peaks at `{python} f"{best['alpha_max']:.0f}"`°. Throw it
flat: `{python} f"{best['launch_angle']:.0f}"`° flies clean,
`{python} f"{after[30]['launch_angle']:.0f}"`° still stalls.

::: {.callout-warning}
## The objective was wrong, not the design
Chapter 01 minimised sink, which drives trim speed as low as it goes — exactly what makes a glider unable to absorb a throw.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## Specified

Asked of the user, 2026-09-04:

1. Fix it so it neither loops nor stalls.
2. Launch speed unchanged at `{python} f"{V_LAUNCH:.0f}"` m/s.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## Assumed

1. **Clean** means α < `{python} f"{CLEAN['alpha']:.0f}"`°, pitch < 180°.
2. Ballast is lead at the extreme nose.
3. Chapter 01's geometry, unchanged.
:::

```{python}
#| label: tbl-fix
#| tbl-cap: "The same airframe before and after the ballast, at each one's best clean launch angle. Pitch excursion is the largest attitude change from level; past 180° the glider has gone over the top."
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
rows = [
    ("trim speed, m/s", f"{opt['V']:.1f}", f"{fixed['V']:.1f}"),
    ("launch ÷ trim", f"{V_LAUNCH/opt['V']:.1f}", f"{V_LAUNCH/fixed['V']:.1f}"),
    ("α max, deg", f"{before['alpha_max']:.0f}", f"{best['alpha_max']:.0f}"),
    ("pitch excursion, deg", f"{turn(before):.0f}", f"{turn(best):.0f}"),
]
print("| | as delivered | + ballast |")
print("|---|---:|---:|")
for name, a, b in rows:
    print(f"| {name} | {a} | {b} |")
```
